data.title: Charles Cannon Brookes Bought 2.7% More Shares In Duke Capital
data.description:

In fact, the recent purchase by Executive Director & Chief Investment Officer Charles Cannon Brookes was not their only acquisition of Duke Capital shares this year. Earlier in the year, they paid UK£0.27 per share in a UK£220k purchase. That means that even when the share price was higher than UK£0.20 (the recent price), an insider wanted to purchase shares. It's very possible they regret the purchase, but it's more likely they are bullish about the company. We always take careful note of the price insiders pay when purchasing shares. It is generally more encouraging if they paid above the current price, as it suggests they saw value, even at higher levels.

Duke Capital insiders may have bought shares in the last year, but they didn't sell any. They paid about UK£0.23 on average. data.title: Koninklijke Vopak N.V. Beat Analyst Estimates: See What The Consensus Is Forecasting For This Year
data.description:
Koninklijke Vopak N.V. (AMS:VPK) shareholders are probably feeling a little disappointed, since its shares fell 2.6% to €53.00 in the week after its latest second-quarter results. Revenues missed analyst forecasts badly, coming in 29% below estimates at €344m. Equally surprising was the fact that statutory earnings per share of €0.89 beat analyst estimates by 16%. This is an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance in its report, look at what experts are forecasting for next year, and see if there has been any change to expectations for the business. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Following last week's earnings report, Koninklijke Vopak's four analysts are forecasting 2026 revenues to be €1.36b, approximately in line with the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are expected to plummet 26% to €3.39 in the same period. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of €1.36b and earnings per share (EPS) of €3.35 in 2026. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

Check out our latest analysis for Koninklijke Vopak

There were no changes to revenue or earnings estimates or the price target of €61.00, suggesting that the company has met expectations in its recent result. It could also be instructive to look at the range of analyst estimates, to evaluate how different the outlier opinions are from the mean. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Koninklijke Vopak at €68.00 per share, while the most bearish prices it at €48.00. There are definitely some different views on the stock, but the range of estimates is not wide enough as to imply that the situation is unforecastable, in our view.

One way to get more context on these forecasts is to look at how they compare to both past performance, and how other companies in the same industry are performing. These estimates imply that revenue is expected to slow, with a forecast annualised decline of 0.9% by the end of 2026. This indicates a significant reduction from annual growth of 0.5% over the last five years. Yet aggregate analyst estimates for other companies in the industry suggest that industry revenues are forecast to decline 4.0% per year. So it's pretty clear that Koninklijke Vopak's revenues are expected to shrink slower than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that there's been no major change in the business' prospects in recent times, with the analysts holding their earnings forecasts steady, in line with previous estimates. On the plus side, they made no changes to their revenue estimates - and they expect it to perform better than the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at €61.00, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price targets.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. We have forecasts for Koninklijke Vopak going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here.

data.title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) Stock Looks Below Fair Value After A 279% Run
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices has surged in recent years on the back of enthusiasm for AI data centers and high performance chips. The real issue for anyone looking at AMD today is whether the cash the business can generate ultimately supports the current share price. A sharp pullback in recent weeks has further focused attention on this question for investors trying to decide how much of AMD's future AI opportunity is already reflected in the valuation.

  • Over the past 3 years the stock has returned about 278.6%, which puts a lot of past optimism on the line if the future cash flows do not match expectations.
  • Record earnings driven by demand for EPYC server processors and Instinct AI accelerators, along with AI focused partnerships and investments, can support expectations for larger data center related cash flows but also raise the bar for how much cash the business needs to produce to keep justifying heavy AI spending and commitments.
  • If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See why Advanced Micro Devices's 95.3x P/E tells a different valuation story.

Does Advanced Micro Devices Look Undervalued on Cash Flow?

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here looks at the cash AMD can return to shareholders over time and then brings those figures back to today. Advanced Micro Devices has generated trailing twelve month free cash flow of about $7.5b, and the projections used in this model assume that this cash figure keeps growing rather than flattening out or shrinking.

Those forecasts build in rising free cash flow through the next decade, which helps explain why the DCF estimate sits meaningfully above the current share price of $449.04. data.title: What Veolia Environnement Holders Got Right
data.description:
If you had been weighing Veolia Environnement in November 2025, you were looking at a utilities group trying to blend big-ticket water and waste projects with higher value technology services, while also carrying sizeable debt and ongoing M&A. Investors who held Veolia Environnement over the past year are up 22.2%, including dividends. The real question now is which of those early trade offs between growth projects, leverage and contract visibility appeared most convincing at the time.

Narratives are how investors here put a case on the record, with explicit assumptions about revenue, margins and the multiple. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

Veolia Environnement has already moved. Pinpoint other ways to investigate the theme among 42 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks.

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing On Veolia Environnement

The shares cost €29.43 at the start of the period, and Veolia Environnement sat between two very different stories about how its water and waste projects might play out.

The bullish narrative put Fair Value at €35.23 and leaned on rising global environmental rules and demand for advanced water and hazardous waste solutions, as well as expected synergies from deals such as Suez and the CDPQ Water Technologies stake.

The bearish view pointed to Fair Value of €25.3 and focused on nearly €21b of net financial debt with leverage around 3 times EBITDA, along with pressure from decentralized energy and local recycling solutions on legacy infrastructure contracts.

What The Results Changed In The Veolia Environnement Debate

Veolia Environnement landing a €1b, 25 year drinking water contract in Spain and closing the Clean Earth acquisition tilted the evidence toward the bullish case that focused on long term water and hazardous waste projects. H1 2026 numbers showed revenue of €22,193m and net income of €671m, both slightly above H1 2025, so profitability expectations were not clearly challenged.

The useful takeaway is about testable assumptions. When a story leans on contract visibility and scale, it helps to track the size and duration of new deals, as well as whether revenue and net income actually move in step with that backlog story.

What Today's Veolia Environnement Price Already Assumes

Veolia Environnement now trades at €33.78, with this selected Narrative arguing that its Fair Value sits below the current level. The focus is not on contracts already won, but on how reliably higher margin activities can turn into lasting profitability.

To judge whether today’s price stacks up, you would need to test one core assumption. The business has to convert its mix of water, hazardous waste, bioenergy and digital efficiencies into sustained margin gains that comfortably absorb input cost shocks and integration risks.

"Key Takeaways: Bearish analysts expect Veolia Environnement's push into higher margin international and booster activities to be undermined by rising input costs and geopolitical disruptions, such as the recent Middle East driven squeeze on fuel and chemical costs that weighed on EBITDA in H1 2026. The main thing that has to go right is that Veolia Environnement turns its growing mix of water, hazardous waste, bioenergy and digital efficiencies into sustained margin gains and earnings growth that offset integration risks from acquisitions like Clean Earth and higher leverage."

Not everyone reads the same price the same way. → See the lower figure this Narrative lands on, and how it gets there

Veolia Environnement And Reliable Power

Looking at Veolia Environnement, you focus on pipes, contracts and physical waste. One step away sits a quieter question. Where does firm, steady electricity come from for energy heavy users?

Some developers are working on compact fission units that run continuously. They aim to build, own and operate these assets, then sell long term power.

Alongside that, they are trying to recycle used nuclear material into fresh fuel. The goal is a more controlled fuel supply and clearer future unit costs.

There is even a second business line in high value isotopes for medicine and industry. If those projects reach commercial scale, your map of essential infrastructure suppliers might look very different.
